Onuskis Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Panevėžio apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Onuskis's Jewish traders relied heavily on business from nearby Latvians, since no border then separated Lithuania from Latvia's Courland region; the community was divided into separate Hasidic and Mitnagdim congregations. By 1941, economic decline and emigration — many to America and South Africa — had reduced the community to about 25 families; the exact location of their murder that year is unknown, and it remains unclear whether it happened locally or alongside the Jews of Rokiskis or Obeliai. Onuskis produced two remarkable figures: Hirsch Lekert, a shoemaker and Bund member who was executed in 1902 after shooting Vilnius's Governor-General in protest of the violent suppression of a May Day demonstration, becoming a significant symbol in Jewish labor history; and Rabbi Abraham Dov Popel, who went on to serve in Lithuania's first parliament after independence in 1918.
